pairedSources.english: We all know that code comments are essential to a well-documented API. But what precisely is a “good” comment? Earlier in this chapter, we identified two major audiences for reference documentation: seekers and stumblers. Seekers know what they want; stumblers don’t. The key win for seekers is a consistently commented codebase so that they can quickly scan an API and find what they are looking for. The key win for stumblers is clearly identifying the purpose of an API, often at the top of a file header. We’ll walk through some code comments in the subsections that follow. The code commenting guidelines that follow apply to C++, but similar rules are in place at Google for other languages.
